A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViewSpatial-Bench and MVSM study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms and Appendices A–C are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, MVSM fine-tuning results and transfer experiments in Tables 1–2, together with qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations in Tables 2–3 and adds training-format and backbone experiments in Appendix C.3 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The proposed annotation algorithms and MVSM fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged, including the frozen vision encoder and projector. v2 adds experimental answer-format and backbone variants without replacing the primary method or introducing an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ScanNet, MS-COCO and Spatial-MM sources, five ViewSpatial-Bench tasks, two VSI-Bench subtasks and indoor/outdoor VSI-App scenarios. The larger stated VSI-App sample count and additional training configurations do not establish new domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds GPT-4o to the quantitative VSI-Bench and VSI-App comparisons; v1 Table 2 compares only Qwen2.5-VL-3B and MVSM. GPT-4o already appeared in the main benchmark and qualitative examples, but its participation in these quantitative transfer comparisons is new.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds controlled multiple-choice versus direct-answer training and fine-tuning experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-2B. Appendix B.4 also revises VSI-App from 50 scenes, split 25/25, to 200, split 100/100. These substantially extend the evaluation design, although Section 5.3.1 still states 50 scenes, leaving the precise setting of the revised transfer results inconsistently documented.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 and Table 6 test whether gains depend on multiple-choice shortcuts and whether training benefits extend across backbones and model sizes. These add substantive controlled robustness evidence beyond v1's transfer experiments and qualitative perspective-confusion analysis. The earlier qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 newly states that each model is evaluated five times on ViewSpatial-Bench and reported scores are averages. v1 does not disclose this practice there; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs. VSI-App's five option-order tests and voting remain unchanged, and neither version reports confidence intervals or run variability.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores are unchanged between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2. New Table 6 reports 79.34% for direct-answer training, 83.01% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B MVSM and 76.45% for InternVL2.5-2B MVSM. Transfer results add GPT-4o and replace VSI-App indoor/outdoor/overall scores: Qwen3B changes from 24/20/22 to 18/27/22.5, and MVSM from 44/24/34 to 41/36/38.5. Given the revised sample count, these are replaced results rather than established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the head-to-body angular-offset calculation and coordinate-to-direction mapping remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same benchmark, annotation-pipeline and MVSM contributions, including the 46.24-point improvement claim. Additional validation does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly interprets the format experiment as evidence against multiple-choice shortcut learning and the backbone experiments as evidence of architecture-independent applicability. Appendix B.2 also replaces the description of balanced directional frequencies with primary-direction dominance interpreted as natural spatial-language usage. The limitations in Appendix A remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub access link and discloses default API parameters and default Transformers generation settings in Appendix C.2. The PDFs do not verify repository contents or availability. Existing training hardware, batch size, epochs and time are moved from Section 5.1 to Appendix C.1 without substantive changes.

R1.justification: New Table 1 provides a structured comparison with eight spatial benchmarks. v2 adds citations for All-Angles Bench, GSR-Bench, STI-Bench and Transformers, while removing several references, including Attention Is All You Need and the spatial-frame-of-reference study. The central positioning around insufficient multi-perspective evaluation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related-work prose, makes local terminology and typo corrections, moves distribution discussion to Appendix B.2 and training details to Appendix C.1, and adds Appendix C.3. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds benchmark-comparison and robustness tables, adds a row to the transfer table, redraws the directional-distribution and object-frequency plots, and revises the word cloud. The distribution figure moves to the appendix, and the retained example figures are grouped on the final page. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new format controls and additional-backbone experiments strengthen validation beyond v1's single trained backbone, while evaluation disclosures improve transparency. These benefits are limited by inconsistent VSI-App reporting: Section 5.3.1 retains 50 scenes and gains of +20/+4, whereas Appendix B.4 states 200 scenes and Table 3 gives +23/+9. The added validation supports a modest net improvement, but the revised transfer evidence is less clearly documented.
